plan_a_advantages: Includes a dedicated hill session for trail-specific power development.
Features a longer, sustained long run (67 minutes) to build endurance.
Prioritizes aerobic consistency and controlled load throughout the week.
plan_b_advantages: Incorporates a tempo run, which can be beneficial for speed work.
Includes a strength session focused on leg muscles and hill work, though less emphasized than in Plan A.
reasoning: For a trail runner aiming to become faster, Plan A is the superior choice. It incorporates a dedicated hill session and a longer, more sustained long run, both crucial for developing the specific power and endurance needed for trail racing. Plan B, while including a tempo run, lacks the focused climbing work and longer, lower-intensity runs that build the foundational aerobic capacity and trail-specific strength that a faster runner requires. Plan A’s structure prioritizes building a stronger aerobic base and trail-specific power, which are more directly linked to speed improvements than Plan B’s approach.
